title: "I played the song": Sneako plays Ye's controversial track 'HH' while heading to UN protest against Netanyahu - NewsBreak
text:
By Anuj Singh Kushwaha ,
1 days ago
Sneako at WrestleMania After Dark Las Vegas Hall Of Fame event at LIV Nightclub on April 19, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada - Source: Getty © Getty Images Sneako at WrestleMania After Dark Las Vegas Hall Of Fame event at LIV Nightclub on April 19, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada - Source: Getty
Kick streamer Sneako played Ye's controversial track "HH" as he headed to a protest outside the UN against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
According to The Guardian, on Thursday, hundreds of protesters gathered outside UN headquarters in NYC ahead of Netanyahu's speech to voice support for Palestine and oppose the Israeli leader. Sneako, a vocal critic of Israel and Netanyahu, also went to the protest. The Kick streamer was accompanied by boxer and streamer Slim Albaher. On their way to the UN, Sneako played Kanye West's 2025 song "HH," which many platforms took down for its alleged antisemitic lyrics.
A clipper account, @Goatedko, posted on X a clip from Slim’s Kick stream showing Sneako swaying to the song in the back seat of a car. Later in the day, Sneako reshared the post and wrote :
"I played the song."
Sneako later posted pictures from the protest on X. The streamer also targeted Israel in his X posts and stream on Thursday.
On Thursday, as soon as the Israeli PM took the stage to begin his speech, delegates from many countries walked out of the UN General Assembly. The moment made headlines worldwide. Sneako reacted to the mass walkout faced by Netanyahu in a tweet, remarking :
"The whole world despises them."
Sneako gives rare praise to Hasan Piker after Netanyahu mentions him in UN speech According to the New York Post, during his UN address, Netanyahu slammed NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who often accuses the Israeli PM of committing a "genocide." Benjamin Netanyahu alleged that under Mamdani's administration, Jews in NYC "no longer feel safe." He also criticized the mayor for his ties to controversial left-wing streamer Hasan Piker. Netanyahu said:
"You praise criminals convicted of supporting Hamas. You count as friends people like Hasan Piker who said, 'America deserved 9/11.'"
In his Thursday stream, Sneako reacted to Netanyahu name-dropping the Twitch streamer in his UN speech. According to a video X account @dailysneako shared, Sneako, who otherwise clashes with Hasan Piker over ideologies, said:
"Rare Hasan Piker W. A lot of stuff he gets wrong... I'm not gonna mince words... But Bibi did mention Hasan Piker during his speech, I think by name. So I've got to give credit where it's due. W. I'm gonna say it... I gotta be consistent. I wanna be attacked in a Bibi speech like that. That's undeniably aura. That's aura... One of the worst people in the world hates you. You gained aura."
Elsewhere on stream, Sneako pushed back against Netanyahu’s accusation about Zohran Mamdani making New York City Jews feel unsafe as mayor. The Kick streamer said:
"Well, Bibi, as a 12% Yehud- I'm 12% Yehudi- I feel completely safe. Mamdani loves and respects the Jewish community. As a representative of the Jewish community in New York, I have nothing but praise for Mamdani, the GOAT. We feel safe. We feel protected."
